deep.reconstruction: Setting (cote 151, 'topos stratifié'). X is a stratified space with strata X_i^* indexed by a poset I. X_i is the closed union of the strata below i, and the ordering satisfies X_i ⊂ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j. For i ≤ j, V_{i,j} is the germ, along X_i^*, of the subspace X_i^* ∪ X_j^* (a germ of tubular neighbourhood of stratum i inside stratum j). V^*_{i,j} = V_{i,j} ∩ X_j^* is the corresponding deleted neighbourhood, i.e. the 'link' piece of X_j^* near X_i^*. The previous page assembled the diagrams (17): V*_{ij} → V_{ij} ← X_i^*, V*_{ij} → X_j^*, all mapping to X. These were indexed by Δ_0 (strata) and Δ_1 (pairs i ≤ j). Grothendieck asked whether the 'sum' diagram has a cocartesian square. On this page he first remarks that gluing the pieces of (17) need not return a space homeomorphic to X; he gives a parenthetical example that is unreadable. He then introduces three-index germs V^j_{i,h} for flags i ≤ j ≤ h; these are the Δ_2-level pieces. He notes that, being germs of subspaces of X, the only canonical morphisms among them are inclusions. The question becomes combinatorial: for which index data (18)-(19) is V^j_{i,h} ⊂ V^{j'}_{i',h'}? The same question is asked for the elementary pieces X_i^*, V^*_{i,j}, V_{i,j}. He assumes all X_i^* ≠ ∅ and records that the cases with empty strata raise questions. Since strata are disjoint, there are no inclusions X_i^* ⊂ X_{i'}^* for i ≠ i'. If V_{i,j} ⊂ V_{i',j'}, comparing the 'points' in X of the two germs (their supports X_i^*, X_{i'}^*) forces i = i'. Then, plausibly, the germ along X_i^* determines X_j, which forces j = j'. If V*_{ij} ⊂ V*_{i'j'}, comparing adherent points ('pts d'adhérence') locates the support between closure(X_i^*) and X_j, and also between closure(X_{i'}^*) and X_{j'}. This leads, on the next page and under the reasonable assumption closure(X_i^*) = X_i, to i ≤ i' and then i = i', j = j'. The upshot (next page) is that the only morphisms among the 'topos-pièces élémentaires' are X_i^* → V_ij, V*_ij → X_j^* and V*_ij → V_ij. This fixes the shape of the indexing category for a dévissage of the stratified space or topos into elementary pieces: strata, tubular germs and links.
errors: The step from V_{i,j} ⊂ V_{i',j'} to j = j' rests on an unproved 'bien vraisemblable' assumption that the germ along X_i^* determines X_j. It can fail without regularity conditions, e.g. if X_j^* does not actually approach X_i^*, making the germ empty or degenerate.

The argument for V* inclusions (completed next page) uses that j is an immediate successor of i. However, (14) on the previous page indexes over all pairs i ≤ j, so the argument is incomplete for non-adjacent pairs. The hypothesis closure(X_i^*) = X_i (frontier condition) is also only assumed as 'raisonnable'.
Non-emptiness of the strata is imposed ad hoc. With empty strata the germs V_{ij} or V*_{ij} can be empty, and inclusions between distinct pieces become trivially possible.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a stratified space into elementary pieces: strata X_i^*, tubular germs V_{ij}, deleted germs or links V*_{ij}, and higher flag germs V^j_{i,h}. These are indexed by Δ_0, Δ_1, Δ_2 of the stratification poset and glued by a cocartesian-type diagram.
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / exit-path category; 'unzipping' and link decompositions of conically stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths, 2000s); Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (links/unzipping, 2010s); Thom-Mather control data
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches dévissage of tame stratified structures via tubular neighbourhoods, but without this combinatorics

ideas.what: Determination that the only canonical morphisms among the pieces are inclusions, and that they reduce to X_i^*→V_ij, V*_ij→X_j^*, V*_ij→V_ij. This fixes the shape of the indexing category.
ideas.modern_name: shape of the gluing diagram for recollement along strata (Δ_1-level link diagram)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in recollement (SGA4 / BBD) and in exit-path descriptions

ideas.what: Observation that gluing the pieces of (17) need not recover a space homeomorphic to X.
ideas.modern_name: failure of strict pushout reconstruction; need for homotopy colimit or regularity conditions

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins describing the full indexing category for a 'pièces élémentaires' dévissage, including Δ_2-level germs V^j_{i,h} for flags i≤j≤h. He asks exactly when V^j_{i,h} ⊂ V^{j'}_{i',h'}, but the three-index case is posed and not resolved here. This anticipates the role of iterated links indexed by flags (the subdivision of the stratification poset) in modern exit-path and unzipping theory.
missed.quote: à quelle condition ... V^j_{i,h} ⊂ V^{j'}_{i',h'} pour i ≤ j ≤ h, i' ≤ j' ≤ h' donnés?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly interesting historically, as a topos-theoretic precursor of flag-indexed link decompositions (Ayala-Francis-Tanaka, Lurie HA A.6). Mathematically it is superseded.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but largely routine combinatorial check on which inclusions can exist between strata, tubular germs and links. The broader programme (stratified dévissage via links) is foreshadowed in Esquisse and now well developed by others. The flag-level germs are a nice anticipation, but the page has no finished result.
transcription_corrections: The germs are written V (V^j_{i,h}, V_{i,j}, V^*_{i,j}), not U, consistent with the previous and next pages.
'les "pts" {+dans X''+}' should be 'les "pts" {+dans X+}', i.e. points in X of these germs.
'Si V_{i,j} ⊂ V_{i',j'}, prises aux "pts" dans X de ces germes, il faut avoir X_i^* ⊂ X_{i'}^* d'où i=i'' is a more plausible reading of that passage.

The line 'Je vais supposer ... X_i^* ≠ ∅' is followed by '(cas où on aurait X_i^* = ∅ questions...)'. The marginal word before 'X_i ⊂ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j' appears to be 'Cette' (struck or partial), probably introducing the convention.
'Il n'y a donc pas de relations d'inclusions entre les X_i^* pour des indices distincts' is confirmed.
The final lines read 'compris entre closure(X_i^*) et X_j ... closure(X_{i'}^*) et X_{j'}, donc aux relations d'inclusions,' continuing onto the next page.
